title: Greatness
note: Greatness is the nature of the great, shown in doing what is hard, lacking arrogance and not speaking of others’ faults. These arise only where you don’t fall from your standing, so it follows honour.

couplets.plain: A person’s light is a wealth of spirit. A person’s disgrace is to say, “I can live without that.”
couplets.pm: A person’s light is the great drive that resolves to do what others can’t. A person’s stain is resolving to leave that undone and simply stay alive. The hard things here are boundless helpfulness and giving. Light means standing out while you live.

links.quote: A person’s light is a wealth of spirit
links.reason: Makes a wealth of spirit the light a person has, which is what this chapter calls greatness.

links.quote: A person’s disgrace is to say, “I can live without that.”
links.reason: Names disgrace as a single thought: that you can live without such spirit.
Makes a wealth of spirit the very thing that gives a person their light.

couplets.plain: Birth is the same for every living being. Distinction is not, because what they do is different.
couplets.pm: All people share the same nature of birth, but the qualities of greatness and smallness are not equal, because their deeds differ. Every varna alike is joined by karma to a body of the five elements and lives out its fruits, so birth is the same. The deeds that test greatness differ with each varna and each body.

links.quote: because what they do is different
links.reason: Birth makes no difference between living beings. What each one does decides their distinction.

couplets.plain: Those who aren’t high aren’t high, even sitting high. Those who aren’t low aren’t low, even sitting low.
couplets.pm: Those who stay small because they can’t do what is hard are not great, even on a raised couch. Those made great by doing it are not small, even on bare low ground. Sitting high and low mean wealth and poverty. So greatness doesn’t come from wealth alone, as the last couplet showed it doesn’t come from birth alone.

couplets.plain: As with women of undivided heart, greatness too comes only if you guard yourself.
couplets.pm: Women of undivided heart guard themselves and don’t slip from their firmness, and so chastity arises. Greatness too arises in a man who guards himself and doesn’t slip from his firmness. To do this is to restrain mind, speech and body and go on doing helpful deeds.

links.quote: greatness too comes only if you guard yourself
links.reason: Gives its one condition: greatness is there only if you guard yourself.
Holds up women of undivided heart, who guard themselves, as the model for keeping greatness.

couplets.plain: The great will carry out hard deeds, and by the right means.
couplets.pm: Those who have become great in this way can, even when they have grown poor, keep to deeds that others find hard and see them through to the end by the right means. “The great” and “will carry out” show they have done such things before, which is how he gets “even when poor”.

links.quote: The great will carry out hard deeds
links.reason: Marks the great by the hard deeds they can finish, by the right means.

couplets.plain: It never enters the minds of the small to say, “We will honour the great and hold on to them.”
couplets.pm: The thought of serving the great and taking on their nature doesn’t arise in the minds of the small. Those who admire themselves merely for having birth, wealth or learning can’t serve the ones who take these calmly as their nature, and so can’t gain that quality.

links.quote: It never enters the minds of the small

couplets.plain: Even distinction, when it falls to the unworthy, turns to nothing but excess.
couplets.pm: Distinction means superiority in birth, wealth or learning. In the great who suit it, it brings calm. If it lands on the small who don’t suit it, it gives that up and produces only greater arrogance.

links.quote: when it falls to the unworthy, turns to nothing but excess
links.reason: Distinction in unworthy hands turns to nothing but excess.

couplets.plain: Greatness always bends low. Smallness admires itself and dresses itself up.
couplets.pm: The great stay calm and free of arrogance even when they have distinction. The small, even without it, admire themselves and dress themselves up, claiming some superiority over others. Some read this as wonder at the way of the world, where the high stoop and the low climb.

links.quote: Smallness admires itself and dresses itself up
links.reason: Smallness has to admire itself and dress itself up.

couplets.plain: Greatness is having no pride. Smallness is riding on pride, all the way to its limit.
couplets.pm: The quality of greatness is to have no arrogance even when there is cause for it, seeing distinction as natural. The quality of smallness is to mount arrogance even without cause and stay at its furthest limit.

links.reason: Measures greatness by having no pride at all.

links.quote: Smallness is riding on pride, all the way to its limit
links.reason: Shows smallness riding on pride, all the way to its limit.

couplets.plain: Greatness hides another’s shame. Smallness speaks of nothing but faults.
couplets.pm: The great speak only of another’s honour and hide their dishonour. The small hide another’s good qualities and speak only of their faults.

links.quote: Smallness speaks of nothing but faults
links.reason: Smallness has only faults to talk about.

ideaLinks.quote: Greatness always bends low. Smallness admires itself and dresses itself up.
ideaLinks.reason: Three couplets set them head to head: bending low against self-admiring, free of pride against riding on it, hiding shame against telling faults.
